en: גַּז, (גַּס) m. (dialect. = עַז, compare Biblical Hebrew equivalent עזניה) gaz, name of a bird of prey, supposed to be the falcon. Chullin III, 1 הגז Arukh (ed. הגס). Tosefta ib. III, 3 הגס. [Alleged name of a species of bees, see הִגְזִין or חִגְזִין.]

גַּס III, גַּסָּה f. (גסס, compare גשש) bulky, huge, large. Chullin III, 1 עוף הגס large fowl (goose, hen &c.), opposed דק.—(בהמה)גסה large cattle (beeves &c.), opposed דקה sheep, goats &c. Ib. Yerushalmi Pesachim IV, 30ᵈ bottom of page; and from—Demai II, 4 sq. במדה ג׳, בגסה in large quantities, wholesale.—Berakhot 6ᵇ פסיעה ג׳ large, hasty step. Pesachim 107ᵇ אכילה ג׳ a large, full meal.—Sheviit IV, 1 (to gather wood or stones) את הגס הגס the larger the better, i.e. picking out the largest for using them in buildings &c., clearly indicating that it is not done for the purpose of improving the field; explained Yerushalmi ib. beginning 35ᵃ כדרך שהוא מלקט … בין דקים לגסים as one gathers in his neighbor’s field distinguishing between the small and large pieces.—Niddah 2ᵇ הַגַּס הַגַּס she noticed the menstruation only when coming in large quantities (in clods, while the blood had previously been imperceptibly gathering).—plural גַּסִּים, גַּסִּין, f. גַּסּוֹת. Yerushalmi Sheviit l. common gender. Chagigah 26ᵃ; and from—גַּס רוּחַ presumptuous, haughty. Pirkei Avot IV, 7. [Ib. גס לבו, see גּוּס.]—plural גַּסֵּי רוח. Yerushalmi Pesachim V, 32ᵃ bottom of page; and from—גַּסִּים (subaudi נקבים) movement of the bowels, see גָּדוֹל end. Yerushalmi Berakhot II, 4ᵈ top; and e.

דַּק I m. (Biblical Hebrew; דקק) thin, fine, tender, opposed גַּס. Chullin III, 1 עוף הד׳ small fowl (doves, birds &c.). Ib. VI, 7 זבל הד׳ powdered ordure, חול הד׳ fine sand; and from—plural דַּקִּים, דַּקִּין. Ib. III, 1; and from הד׳ the small bowels.—Yerushalmi Berakhot II, 4ᵈ top בדקים (subaudi נקבים) concerning the smaller functions of the body (urinizing, usually קטנים), opposed גסים (usually גדולים), see גָּדוֹל.—Kelim II, 2 הד׳ שבכלי חרס the fine and small earthen vessels; and from—Fem. דַּקָּה. (בהמה) ד׳, small cattle, see גַּס. Chullin l. common gender. Bava Kamma VII, 7. Ib. 80ᵃ חיה ד׳ small forest animals (deer, fox &c.). בד׳ (subaudi מדה) in small quantities, retail. Demai II, 5; Yerushalmi ib. 23ᵃ bottom of page; Tosefta ib. III, 12, see לוּמָּא.—Yoma IV, 4 ד׳ powdered frank incense, ד׳ מן הד׳ the very finest; and from—plural דַּקּוֹת. Chullin 56ᵃ; and from

דָּרַס
1) to tread, stamp. Bava Kamma II, 1 דָּרְסָה על וכ׳ if she trod upon a vessel. Yerushalmi Ma'asrot II, 49ᵈ bottom of page והוא עתיד לדוֹרְסָן dates which he intends to stamp; and from—בית הדּוֹרְסִין, see מַעֲגִיל.—Part. pass. דָּרוּס, f. דְּרוּסָה.—דְּרוּסַת איש (calcata a viro) deflowered. Ketubot I, 7.

—2) (ritual) to press, i.e. to cut the throat of an animal by pressing the knife (adding muscular force to the cutting capacity of the knife, instead of passing the latter to and back). Chullin 20ᵇ. Ib. 30ᵇ שמא יִדְרוֹסוּ זה על זה lest they press the knife by one adding to the strength of the other.—Denom. דְּרָסָה.

—3) (of animals of prey) to attack with paws or claws. Ib. 53ᵃ. Pesachim 49ᵇ; Sanhedrin 90ᵇ; and from—Chullin III, 6 עוף הַדּוֹרֵס a bird of prey (that seizes food with its claws or eats animals before they are dead).—דְּרוּסָה f. an animal known to have been attacked by a beast or bird of prey (which are suspected of leaving a poisonous substance in the body). Chullin III, 1 (42ᵃ) דְּרוּסַת הזאב an animal saved from the attack of a wolf.—יש דרוסה ל־ the case of a d’rusah applies to one attacked by &c. Chullin 52ᵇ; and from

—4) to stuff food into the camel’s mouth, contradistinguished to אָבַס and הִלְעִיט.—Shabbat XXIV, 3; Breishit Rabbah section (Parashah) 63; Bamidabar Rabbah section (Parashah) 21.

Nifal - נִדְרַס to be trodden down, to be effaced (by treading or otherwise). Bava Metzia 22ᵃ עשוי לִידָּרֵס liable to be effaced; ib. 22ᵇ

הֶמְסֵס, מָסָס m. (מָסַס) [the dissolving (digesting) receptacle,] the first stomach of ruminants, compare הַבְלִילָא. Chullin III, 1 המסס (= הַהֶ׳, or הַמָּסָס). Vayikra Rabbah section (Parashah) 4; Midrash Till. to Psalms CIII, beginning המ׳ לטחון the first stomach has the function of grinding (the food). Vayikra Rabbah section (Parashah) 18; Kohelet Rabbah to XII, 3 ‘the grinders’ (ib.) זו ה׳ that is the stomach. [From later usage, e.g. Tur Yoré Deah 49, and from its Chald. equivalent it would seem that our word is הֶמְסֵס, and the definite article fused with the ה of the noun.]

וֶשֶׁט m. (יָשַׁט) [something stretched and narrow,]
1) gullet. Chullin III, 1 נקובת הו׳ an animal whose gullet is found to have been perforated.—Niddah 23ᵇ וֶשְׁטוֹ נקוב if the infant’s gullet is perforated (there being a hole in the throat); ו׳ אטום if its gullet is closed; and from—Yalkut Psalms 687 (translating מלקוחי, Psalms XXII, 16) לוִושְׁטִי; Midrash Till. to Psalms l. common gender. לויסיטי (correct accordingly; compare Lat. fauces) to my throat.

—2) (compare בְּלוּעָה, בְּלִיעֵי) straits, canal. Berakhot 8ᵃ (Rashi: loop-hole for the rope), see פִּיטוּרִין and צִיפּוּרִין; Moʿed Katan end; Vayikra Rabbah section (Parashah) 4; Midrash Tanḥuma Mikk. 10; ed. Bub. 15; Kohelet Rabbah to VI, 6.

חָלָל III m. (חָלַל)
1) cavity, empty space, hollow; throat; inside. 'Uktzin II, 8 ממעך את חֲלָלָהּ you squeeze its cavity (compress it); Yerushalmi Yoma VIII, 44ᵈ bottom of page (see Löw, Löw, Aramäische Pflanzennamen, Leipzig 1881 p. 123). Pirkei Avot Zar. 28ᵃ מכה של ח׳ an internal sore (as in the mouth, throat &c.). Yerushalmi ib. II, 40ᵈ top; Yerushalmi Shabbat XIV, 14ᵈ top כל שהוא מן הח׳ ולפנים וכ׳ whatever is in the throat and farther inside may be cured on the Sabbath, opposed to מן השפה; compare Sotah 45ᵇ quot. section (Parashah) see חָלָל I. Chullin III, 1 if the heart is perforated לבית חֲלָלוֹ up to its chamber. Berakhot 19ᵇ ח׳ טפח a hollow space of one hand-breadth. Chullin 44ᵇ. Pesachim 54ᵃ חֲלָלָהּ the formation of its interior; and from—plural חֲלָלִים. Berakhot 60ᵇ, see חָלוּל.

—2) (compare חַלְחוֹלִית) intricacy, devices. Shabbat 11ᵃ חֲלָלָהּ של רשות the devices of political government.

חוּט III m. (Biblical Hebrew; preceding wds.)
1) thread, chord, strap; sinew. Kelim XXIX, 3 ח׳ משקולת chord of the plumb-line; ib. 4 ח׳ מאזנים of the balances.—Yevamot 121ᵇ, and from ח׳ השערה a single hair, see דִּקְדֵּק.—Chullin III, 1, a from ח׳ השדרה the spinal chord.—Chagigah 12ᵇ הקב"ה … ח׳ של חסד the Lord strings around him a chord of grace (protection). Megillah 13ᵃ ח׳ של חסד וכ׳ a chord of (divine) grace was strung &c. Menachot 39ᵃ נפסק הח׳ מעיקרו the twining thread of the show-fringes is broken at the top. Ib. ח׳ של כרך the thread used for twining; and from—Yerushalmi Shabbat VI, 8ᵇ bottom of page חוטמה וכ׳, read: חוט דומה לשערה a band (of hair) resembling her own hair.—plural חוּטִים, חוּטִין. Sanhedrin 52ᵃ, and e. שני ח׳ של אש two threads (lines) of fire. Vayikra Rabbah section (Parashah) 14, see זְהוֹרִית.—Menachot 39ᵇ חוּטֵי צמר woolen threads (as show-fringes). Shabbat VI, 5 חוטי שיער bands made of hair. Ib. 6 בח׳ וכ׳ with threads … in their ears (in place of earrings). Chullin 93ᵃ ח׳ שביד the veins of the fore-foot; and from

—2) (Geogr.) air-line. Tosefta Terumot II, 12. Ib. 13 מן הח׳ ולפנים וכ׳ what is inside (East) of the line is considered as belonging to the land of Israel.—[Tosefta Kelim Bava Batra V, 14 יוצאת החוט, see חוּץ II.]

טְרֵיפָה, טְרֵפָה f. (Biblical Hebrew; טָרַף)
1) an animal torn by a beast of prey. Midrash Till. to Psalms VII, see טֶרֶף.

—2) (ritual law) an animal afflicted with a (fatal) organic disease, the discovery of which, after slaughtering, makes it forbidden, t’refah, (of persons, m.) one having a fatal organic disease (the killing of whom would not be considered murder before the law). Chullin 42ᵃ ט׳ אינה חיה a t’refa animal cannot survive (a year); and from—Sanhedrin 78ᵃ ההורג את הט׳ if one kills a person afflicted with a fatal organic disease; וט׳ שהרג and if such a person committed a murder. Ib. עידי ט׳ witnesses afflicted &c.; and from

—3) organic disease. Vayikra Rabbah section (Parashah) 13 (reference. to החיה, Vayikra XI, 2) החיה מטְרֵיפָתָהּ וכ׳ that which can recover from its disease, you may eat.—plural טְרֵיפוֹת, טְרֵפוֹת. Chullin III, 1; and from—Esp. cases of t’refah, ritual law concerning t’refah. Ib. 48ᵇ; and from

כְּלָל m. (preceding wds.)
1) general rule, principle. Sifra K’dosh., Parah 2, Chaldaic IV (reference. to Vayikra XIX, 18) זה כ׳ גדול וכ׳ this (‘love thy neighbor as thyself’) is the most important principle in the Law. Shabbat VII, 1. Chullin III, 1 זה הכ׳ this is the general rule; and see from—Transferred בִּכְלַל, לִכְלַל under the influence of. Sifré Bamidbar 157 לפי שהיה בכ׳ כעס בא לכ׳ טעות because he was under the influence of anger, he came under the influence of mistaken judgment; Yalkut ib. 786; and from

—2) community. Berakhot 49ᵇ לעולם אל … מן הכ׳ a person must never exclude himself from the community (by saying, ‘Praise ye’, instead of ‘Let us praise’). Mekhilta Bo., Pisḥa, section (Parashah) 18 ולפי שהוציא … מן הכ׳ וכ׳ and as he excluded himself from the community (by saying ‘you’) &c.; and e.

—3) total, sum. Bava Batra 123ᵃ בכְלָלָן אתה וכ׳ as their sum total you find seventy (Breishit XLVI, 27), whereas the detailed record counts only sixty nine.

—4) generalization, statement by implication, opposed פרט specification; inclusion, comprehension under a class. Berakhot 26ᵇ, and from עד ועד בכ׳, see עַד.—Sifra introduction מכ׳ ופרט מפרט וּכְ׳ וכ׳ interpretation based upon a general law followed by specification, or specification followed by generalization. Ib. כל דבר שהיה בכ׳ וכ׳ when a law is once laid down in general, and in another place a specification is given (e.g. Vayikra VII, 37, and ib. 20), it is stated specifically not for its own sake alone, but as applicable to the whole class. Ib. beginning מכ׳ ופרט וּכְ׳ אי אתה דן וכ׳ if a general rule is followed by a specification and this again by a generalization, you must be guided by the specification (e.g. Devarim XIV, 26). Tosefta Sotah VIII, 10; Sotah 37ᵃ ברוך בכ׳ … ארור בכ׳ וכ׳ ‘blessed be’ was pronounced on Mount Gerizim in general (corresp. to the general curse, Devarim XXVII, 26
) and was specified (corresp. to ib. 15—25) ; ‘cursed be’ was pronounced on Mount Ebal in general (ib. 26) &c.; and from—מִכְּ׳ by implication. Nedarim 11ᵃ, and from מכ׳ לאו אתה שומע הן from no you understand yes, see הֵן.—Pesachim 16ᵇ שהותרה מִכְּלָלָהּ וכ׳ which was permitted (dispensed with), by implication, for a community (if unclean, derived from Bamidbar IX, 2, see Pesachim 77ᵃ). Chullin 37ᵇ מכ׳ דטרפה וכ׳ this proves by implication that t’refah is not the same as &c.; and see from—לאו … כ׳ not at all (compare כְּלוּם). Ib. 20ᵇ; and from—[Mekh. Bo, beginning כ׳ לדברות, read: כֶּלִי.]—plural כְּלָלוֹת (fem.). Nazir 48ᵇ. Sotah 37ᵇ. Eruvin 27ᵃ אין למדין מן הכ׳ וכ׳ from general rules (the use of the word כל, as ib. III, 1) we must not derive anything, not even when an exception is stated (as there may be other exceptions); and from—Shemot Rabbah section (Parashah) 32, beginning כְּלָלִים.

כֶּרֶס f. (Biblical Hebrew כֶּרֶשׂ in כְּרֵשׂוֹ; compare כַּרְכְּשָׁא) [bag,] stomach, belly. Taanit 26ᵃ top על נפש … וכ׳ מלאה when the appetite is satisfied and the stomach filled. Shabbat 151ᵇ (reference. to Kohelet XII, 6) זה הכ׳ ‘the pitcher is broken’, that means the stomach. Ib. לאחר שלשה … כְּרֵיסוֹ נבקעת וכ׳ three days after burial one’s stomach bursts open … saying (to the mouth), Take what thou hast put into me; Kohelet Rabbah to l. common gender.; Yerushalmi Yevamot XVI, 15ᶜ bottom of page; Breishit Rabbah section (Parashah) 100. Ketubot 16ᵃ, and from כְּרֵיסָהּ בין שיניה her belly extends to her teeth, i.e. she cannot deny her pregnancy. Kohelet Rabbah to VII, 8 [read:] היה מפעפע בכְרֵיסָהּ כאריסה וכ׳ burned in her stomach like the venom of &c.; [Yerushalmi Sanhedrin X, 28ᵈ top ככריסה, see חֲכִינָה]; and from—Esp. the stomach of ruminants, maw. Chullin III, 1 הכ׳ הפנימית the inner stomach, explained ib. 50ᵇ כל הכ׳ כולו … ואיזהו כ׳ החיצון וכ׳ (masc. !) the whole maw is called the inner stomach, and the outer stomach is the flesh (muscle) which covers the largest portion of the stomach; ib. (another opinion) טפח בוושט סמון לכ׳ וכ׳, corrected; טפח בכ׳ סמוך לוושט one handbreadth of the stomach where it joins the gullet is called the inner stomach; [oth. defin., see אִסְתּוֹמְכָא, דִּיבָא and מֵילַת].—plural כְּרֵיסוֹת. Sukkah 21ᵇ שכְּרֵיסוֹתֵיהֶן רחבות whose bellies are broad (projecting further than the rider’s body; Tosefta Parah III (II), 2 שכְּרֵיסָן רחבה).

כָּבֵד III common gender. (Biblical Hebrew; preceding wds.) [heaviness, seat of anger and melancholy,] liver. Berakhot 61ᵇ top כ׳ כועס ומרה וכ׳ the liver is excited, and the gall pours a drop over it and quiets it. Chullin III, 1 ניטל הכ׳; ib. 2 ניטלה הכ׳ if the liver of an animal is gone. Arakhin V, 2 (20ᵃ) ערך כְּבֵדִי עלי (Bavli ed. כְּבֵידִי) I vow the value of my liver (being a vital organ); and from

כּוֹס I common gender. (Biblical Hebrew; or כנס, see Ges. Thes., and Hebr. Dict.10 section (Parashah) see)
1) cup, also a drink. Tamid III, 4. Eruvin 65ᵇ בג׳ … בכיסו בכוֹסוֹ בכעסו man’s character is found out in three things, in his money bag, in his cup (when drinking) and in his anger; Der. Er. Zutta Chaldaic V.—Ketubot 75Ketubot 75ᵇ, sq., see בָּדַק. Pesachim 105ᵃ קדושה על הכ׳ sanctification (of the Sabbath or Holy Day) over a cup of wine. Ib. אם אין לו אלא כ׳ אחד if he has only enough wine for one cup. Shabbat XIV, 3 כ׳ עיקרים, see עִיקָּר; and from—plural כּוֹסוֹת. Kelim XXII, 1; Yerushalmi Pirkei Avot Zar. II, end, 42ᵃ, see הַנָּחָה. Menachot 28ᵇ, see אֲלֶכְסַנְדְּרִי. Pesachim X, 1, and from ארבע כ׳ four cups of wine to be drunk on the Passover night; and from

—2) cavity. Parah II, 5 (two black or white hairs) בתוך כ׳ אחד in one follicle (see גוּמָּא).—plural as ab. Ib. Yerushalmi Pirkei Avot Zar. l. common gender. הן כ׳ הן גומות kosoth and gummoth mean the same things.—בֵּית הכּוֹסוֹת the second stomach of ruminants. Chullin III, 1 (42ᵃ), see comment. and הַבְלִילָא. Chullin 49ᵃ; 50ᵇ עובי בית הכ׳ the folds (thick walls) of the etc.; and from

מָרָה I f. (Biblical Hebrew)
1) fem. of מַר II, bitter.

—2) bitter taste. Yerushalmi Berakhot VI, 10ᵃ בטלה מָרָתָן their bitter taste is gone.

—3) drop, poison (see אֶרֶס). Terumot VIII, 5 המ׳ the serpent’s discharge.—Esp. gall, bile. Chullin III, 1; and from—Bava Metzia 107ᵇ (reference. to Shemot XXIII, 25) זו מ׳ that means (overflow of) bile, see חָלָה.—Transferred austerity, gravity. Shir HaShirim Rabbah to IV, 4 (play on מֹרִיָּה) שממנו יוצאת מ׳ לעולם (not יוצא) from it austerity (responsibility) went forth to the world. Ketubot 103ᵇ זרוק מ׳ בתלמידים cast bile among the students (be austere against them). Sifré Devarim 323 (reference. to Devarim XXXII, 32 אשכלת מררת) הגדולים שבכם מָרָתָן פרוסה בכם כאשכל as to the great among you, their bile (austere rebuke) is distributed among you as the juice in the grapes; Yalkut ib. 946 מרתן פרוסה בהן וכ׳ their bile is distributed within them.

מוֹחַ m. (Biblical Hebrew מֹחַ; מחח , see מָהָה) marrow, especially (with or without ראש) brain. Tosefta Pesachim VI, 10, see קוּלִית. Chullin III, 1 קרום של מ׳ the membrane which surrounds the brain, see חַיִּיתָא IV. Ib. 45ᵃ מ׳ כל מה … מ׳ as to moaḥ, whatever is contained in the skull is considered as brain. Ib. 45ᵇ רוב מוֹחוֹ the larger part of the marrow of the spine (spinal cord); and from—Menachot 80ᵇ; Yevamot 9ᵃ אין לו מ׳ בקדקדו has no brains in his head.
נֵץ II m. (Biblical Hebrew; probably from its far-sightedness, , Hifil) hawk. Chullin III, 1; Tosefta ib. III, 3; and e.

נָטַל (Biblical Hebrew; compare טִלְטֵל)
1) to move, carry off; to receive, take. Bava Metzia I, 1 זה נוֹטֵל וכ׳ the one (of the claimants) gets three shares &c. Yerushalmi Sotah I, 16ᵈ bottom of page, and e. ומה שכר נָטְלוּ על כך what reward did they get for it?—Sifra Sh’mini, beginning מסיני נטלו להם they got (their punishment) from Sinai. Shabbat 151ᵇ טוֹל מה וכ׳ take away what thou hast put into me. Arakhin 16ᵇ; Bava Batra 15ᵇ טול קיסם מבין עיניך (Agadoth hat-Torah (quoted in Rabbinowicz Variæ Lectiones). שיניך) remove the chip from between thy eyes (teeth); טול קורה וכ׳ remove the beam from &c. Gittin VI, 1 אף האומרת טול לי גטי even if she says, get me my letter of divorce (instead of ‘receive for me’). Ib. 78ᵃ טְלִי גיטיך וכ׳ take up thy letter of divorce from the ground. Pesikta d'Rav Kahana R. section (Parashah) 26, end נָטַלְתִּי עיני I lifted up my eyes. Berakhot II, 8 לא כל הרוצה לִיטּוֹל לו את השם יִטּוֹל Yerushalmi ed., not every one who desires to assume a name, may assume it, i.e. not every one has a right to consider himself superior to the masses (see יוֹהֲרָא); and see from—Part. pass. נָטוּל; f. נְטוּלָה removed. Nedarim XI, 12 (if a woman says) נ׳ אני מן היהודים I will be removed from (keep no company with) Jews; יפר … ותהא נ׳ וכ׳ the husband may forbid the vow as far as it concerns himself, and (for the rest) let her be isolated &c.—Sanhedrin 21ᵇ נְטוּלֵי טחול persons who had their milt cut out (to make them fast runners).—V. נְטוּלָה.

—2) (subaudi מים) to pour water over one’s hands for purification; נ׳ לידים, (elliptically) נ׳ ידים, or only נ׳ to wash the hands before and after meals, before prayer &c. Tosefta Yadayim I, 1 מי רביעית נוֹטְלִין לידים וכ׳ (Variant ed. Zuckermandel (see Tosefefta), and Mishnah ib. Yerushalmi Ketubot XII, 35ᵃ top; Yerushalmi Kilayim IX, 32ᵇ top; (Breishit Rabbah section (Parashah) 100 נקופה), see אָרוֹן. —3) to point out, to pronounce. Ib. אימא פרושי שמיה חוא I might say, noḳeb means uttering His name (the Tetragrammaton)? סִימְפּוֹן, סִמְ׳ m. (= סנפון; סָנַף) [ramification, interweaving,]
1) ramified blood-vessel, artery; bronchiae. Yerushalmi Megillah I, 71ᶜ bottom of page היה עשוי כמין ס׳ if the writing was done in the shape of arteries (furcated); compare חֲלִיטָה I.—Chullin 49ᵃ (explained בית הסימפונות, see infra) ס׳ גדול the main branch (of the aorta); and e.—plural סִימְפּוֹנוֹת, סִמְ׳. Ib. III, 1 עד שתינקב לבית הס׳ until the perforation of the lungs reaches the starting point of the ramified blood-vessels (see supra), explained ib. 45ᵇ להיכא דשפכי ס׳ כולהו into which all the vessels discharge themselves.

—2) [cross-writing,] postscript to a document, codicil, conditions or modifications attached to a deed; receipt in full or in participle Yerushalmi Gittin VII, end, 49ᵃ; Yerushalmi Kiddushin III, 64ᵃ top; Yerushalmi Eruvin III, 21ᵇ top סדר ס׳ כך הוא וכ׳ this is the formula of a simpon (of betrothal), I—betroth thee—, with the condition that I marry thee on a certain day, and if that day arrives and I fail to marry thee, I shall have no claim &c. Ib. ירדו לס׳ בשיטת וכ׳ they entered into a conditional agreement in accordance with the principle of R. M. &c. (i.e. stating both alternatives), see תְּנַאי. Yerushalmi Bava Metzia X, 17ᶜ ס׳ כתוב מלעיל וס׳ וכ׳ if one postscript is written at the top of the document, and one effaced at the bottom. Bava Metzia I, 8 (20ᵃ) אם יש עמהן ס׳ יעשה מה שבס׳ Yerushalmi ed. and Manuscript Munich (Bavli and Mishnah ed. plural) if a postscript is attached to the documents, you must be guided by the postscript. Ib. 20ᵇ ס׳ היוצא וכ׳ a postscript (receipt to a note) produced by the creditor. Ib. 21ᵃ ס׳ שיש עליו עדים a receipt signed by witnesses; and from—plural as ab. Bava Metzia I, 8, see supra.

—3) an implicit condition the non-fulfillment of which annuls the agreement, whence, a bodily defect (of a woman or a slave) not stated in the contract. פָּסַק (Biblical Hebrew פָּשַׂק) [to separate, part, distribute,]
1) to divide, split, interrupt. Taanit 27ᵇ; Megillah 22ᵃ פּוֹסֵק the reader divides (one verse), i.e. the first reads two verses and a half, leaving the other half to be read by his successor. Ib. לא התיר לי לִפְסוֹק וכ׳ he permitted me to cut a verse in two only in teaching the school children. Ib. 31ᵇ במשנה תורה פוסק the chapter in Deuteronomy containing the curses (Devarim XXVIII, 15—69) may be divided (to be read by two or more); and from—[Breishit Rabbah section (Parashah) 10 כיון שפסקה; Yalkut ib. 16 שפוסקה, see פָּתַק.]—Part. pass. פָּסוּק; f. פְּסוּקָה. Chullin III, 3 פְּסוּקַת הגרגרת, see גַּרְגֶּרֶת.

—2) (denominative of פָּסוּק) to recite a verse. Chagigah 15ᵃ, sq. פְּסוֹק לי פְּסוּקְךָ (interch. with Chald. פסוק לי פסוקיך) recite to me thy Bible verse (recently learned).

V, 8 לא פ׳ … אלא וכ׳ only R. Yerushalmi decreed barley as a part of alimentation, because he lived near Edom. Ib. פוסק לעומתן וכ׳ he must give her &c., see עוּמָּה. Ib. VI, 2 הפוסק מעות לחתנו if a man agrees to pay a certain amount to his intended son-in-law (on the date of marriage). Ib. 3 פָּסְקָה להכניס … הוא פוסק וכ׳ if she promises to bring to him one thousand Denars, he must assign to her (as settlement in the K’thubah) fifteen Manehs. Tosefta ib. XIII (XII), 1 אם פָּסְקוּ לה … מה שפסקו פסקו if the court has granted her (alimentation), what they have granted, is granted. Shir HaShirim Rabbah to II, 13 הנִשְׁאָרִים the survivors of the Messianic days; and e.

Piël - שֵׁיאֵר ,) שִׁיֵּיר to leave over, reserve. Bava Batra IX, 6 שכיב … וש׳ וכ׳ if an ill person donated all his property to others and reserved some land for himself, his donation is valid (even if he recovers). Ib. 148ᵃ דקל לאחד וש׳ פירותיו לפניו ש׳ מקום פירי if he donated a palm-tree (for the wood of it) to a person, and reserved its fruit for himself, he meant to reserve for himself the place whereon the fruit grows (the branches). Ib. כל … בעין יפה מְשַׁיֵּיר whatever one reserves for one’s self, one reserves liberally; and see from—Part. pass. מְשׁוֹאָר, (מְשׁוּיָּיר). Yerushalmi Pesachim VII, 35ᵃ top לא עשה בה המש׳ כיוצא the law does not treat that which is left over (of the sacrifice) like that which has been carried outside of its limits. Peah III, 3 נותּן מן המש׳ על מה ששייר he must give to the poor out of the remainder in proportion to that which he left over; נותן מן המש׳ על הכל he must give out of the remainder a quantity corresponding to the whole (including that which he has taken out before); and from

Hifil - הִשְׁאִיר same. Midrash Till. to Psalms IX שלא להַשְׁאִיר זכר וכ׳ that he will not leave a remainder of the memory of Amalek; Yalkut ib. 642 להשאר (correct accordingly); and e.

Nithpaël - נִשְׁתַּיֵּיר to be left over. Chullin III, 1 ניטל … ולא נ׳ וכ׳ if the liver of a slaughtered animal is found consumed without any part of it left. Yoma 77ᵃ לא נִשְׁתַּיְירוּ משונאיהן וכ׳ no remnant or survivor would have been left of the enemies of Israel (euphem. for ‘of Israel’); and from

comments.en: 6) (an animal in which:) the gullet is perforated; most of the windpipe is detached (in its breadth); the spine is broken and the spinal cord is cut; the heart is perforated up to its chamber; the liver is diminished and nothing remains of it; the lung is perforated or diminished (R. Shimon says: until the perforation reaches the bronchiae); the stomach is perforated; the intestines are perforated (R. Yossi b. R. Yehudah says: Even if the gall bladder is perforated, it is unfit);
comments.he: [ו] נקובת הושט ופסוקת הגרגרת ברובה נשברה השדרה ונפסק החוט שלה נקב קרום של מוח נקב הלב לבית חללו נטל הכבד ולא נשתייר הימנו כלום הריאה שנקבה או שחסרה. ר' שמעון אומר עד שתנקב לבית הסמפונות. נקבה הקיבה נקבו הדקים. ריב"י אומר אף נקבה המרה פסולה.

en: 7) the inner stomach (the maw) is perforated or most of the outer stomach is torn (R. Yehudah says: In a large (ox) a handbreadth, and in a small one, the majority [even if it is not a handbreadth]);

8) the omasom and the reticulum is perforated (until its perforation is seen) on the outside; it fell from a roof (even if breaks are not visible from the outside); most of its ribs were broken; it was trodden by a wolf (R. Yehudah says: Being trodden by a wolf, for a small animal, and being trodden by a lion, for a large one); it was trodden by a hawk, for a small bird; it was trodden by a large bird, for a large bird. I might think that if the skull were diminished, but the brain membrane not perforated; if the heart were perforated, but not up to its chamber; if the spine were broken, but the cord not severed; if the liver were diminished, but an olive-size remained of it; if the omasom and the reticulum were perforated into each other;
he: [ז] הכרס הפנימי שנקבה או שנקרע רוב החיצונה. ר' יהודה אומר בגדולה טפח ובקטנה רובה.

[ח] המסס ובית הכוסות שנקבו לחוץ. נפלה מן הגג ונשתברו רוב צלעותיה ודרוסת הזאב בדקה. ר"י אומר דרוסת הזאב בדקה, ודרוסת הארי בגסה, ודרוסת הנץ בעוף הדק, ודרוסת הנס בעוף הגס. יכול אף נפחת הגלגולת ולא ניקב קרום של מוח? נקב הלב ולא לבית חללו? נשברה השדרה ולא נפסק החוט שלה? ניטל הכבד ונשתייר הימנו כזית? המסס ובית הכוסות שנקבו זה לתוך זה?…
